name: Walt Disney World Swan
positioning: A Westin hotel inside Walt Disney World, part of the Swan and Dolphin resort complex designed by Michael Graves, within walking distance of Epcot and Disney's Hollywood Studios
best_for: Families who want to walk to Epcot and Disney's Hollywood Studios
Disney fans who want Early Theme Park Entry
Travelers wanting lake, park or fireworks views from their room

facts.text: The Swan is part of the Walt Disney World Swan and Dolphin resort complex.
The resort was designed by architect Michael Graves in his postmodern style.
On select nights, guests can experience Extended Evening Hours at the Disney parks.
An on-site Disney Planning Center helps with park tickets and dining reservations.
Guests can walk to Disney's BoardWalk Entertainment District.
Mandara Spa has interior gardens, including a Tea Garden and a Meditation Garden.
The resort complex has a white sand beach.
Camp Dolphin is a supervised kids' club for children ages 5 through 12.
Il Mulino New York Trattoria serves seasonal Italian cuisine in a rustic atmosphere.
Guests can play Walt Disney World's three championship golf courses or the nine-hole walking course.
Lagoon is a game room and bowling experience at the resort.

highlights.text: The complex is within walking distance of Epcot and Disney's Hollywood Studios.
Guests get 30-minute Early Theme Park Entry at all four Walt Disney World parks daily.
Some rooms look over Crescent Lake or the Tower of Terror, and a variety of rooms have views of Disney fireworks.
The Grotto Pool has tropical waterfalls, a waterslide and a kiddie pool.
Mandara Spa, inside the Swan and Dolphin, is a Balinese-inspired retreat.

considerations.text: Restaurants, pools and resort experiences are shared across the Swan and Dolphin complex; Camp Dolphin is on the lower level of the Dolphin.
WhataHotel notes the large resort can feel crowded during peak Disney seasons.
